quotes.text: ADF charges per activity run, so every copy activity stored procedure and pipeline execution adds to your bill. Fabric Data Factory uses capacity-based pricing instead.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the core pricing difference between classic ADF and Fabric Data Factory.

quotes.text: If pipelines are the assembly line that moves boxes around, data flow, Gen 2 is the kitchen where you actually chop, season, and cook the raw ingredients.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable analogy separating orchestration from transformation.

quotes.text: Copy jobs are for set it and forget it continues ingestion. You want data flowing in automatically, day after day, with minimal maintenance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear rule for when to choose copy jobs over copy activities.

quotes.text: Mirroring reads the transaction log of your source database. Every change, every insert, update, and delete gets picked up and appears in one lake within minutes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains concisely how mirroring achieves near real-time replication.

quotes.text: The real magic isn't any single tool. It's how they all talk to each other through one lake.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the integration value of the Fabric platform.

chapters.title: How it differs from Azure Data Factory

takeaways: Fabric Data Factory is the built-in data integration engine of Microsoft Fabric, with capacity-based pricing and OneLake as automatic storage instead of linked services and storage accounts.
Pipelines orchestrate, Dataflow Gen2 transforms with Power Query, copy jobs handle continuous incremental ingestion and mirroring replicates operational databases in near real time.
If your ADF bill is low and you are not on Fabric, staying with ADF can make sense; if you already have Fabric capacity, pipelines cost very little extra.
hook: Is Fabric Data Factory just Azure Data Factory with a new name? This episode explains the four building blocks - pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, copy jobs and mirroring - and how they work together through OneLake. Data engineers and analysts get a clear rule of thumb for when switching from ADF pays off.
